1	# Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://climate.nasa.gov/vital-signs/carbon-dioxide/ and Our World in Data — CO₂ and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Global Carbon Budget 2025)
     5	
     6	## Atmospheric CO₂ Concentration
     7	
     8	The latest measurement from NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory (February 2026) records atmospheric CO₂ at **429 parts per million (ppm)**. This represents a more than 50% increase from the pre-industrial baseline of approximately 280 ppm. The current level is at least 1.5 times greater than the natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago — a change that took thousands of years then but has occurred in roughly two centuries now. Ground-based and satellite measurements confirm the sharp acceleration, linked primarily to the burning of coal, oil, and natural gas.
     9	
    10	## Global Emissions Trajectory (1750–2024)
    11	
    12	Before the Industrial Revolution, CO₂ emissions were negligible. Growth remained relatively slow until the mid-20th century. In **1950**, the world emitted roughly **6 billion tonnes** of CO₂. By **1990**, emissions had nearly quadrupled to over **20 billion tonnes**. Today, global annual emissions from fossil fuels and industry exceed **35 billion tonnes**. While emissions growth has slowed in recent years, they have not yet peaked.
    13	
    14	![Annual CO₂ emissions by country](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    15	
    16	## Who Emits the Most? Country-Level Totals
    17	
    18	China is the world's largest emitter by a significant margin, producing over 12 billion tonnes annually — more than one-quarter of the global total. The United States peaked near 6 billion tonnes around 2005 and has since declined to roughly 5 billion tonnes. India has risen rapidly to approximately 3 billion tonnes. Europe's share has fallen substantially.
    19	
    20	| Country / Region | Approx. Annual CO₂ (billion t) | Share of Global | Trend (recent) |
    21	|---|---|---|---|
    22	| China | ~12.5 | ~27% | Slight increase |
    23	| United States | ~5.0 | ~14% | Declining |
    24	| India | ~3.0 | ~8% | Rising |
    25	| EU-27 | ~2.7 | ~7% | Declining |
    26	| Germany | ~0.6 | ~1.7% | Declining |
    27	| United Kingdom | ~0.3 | ~0.9% | Declining |
    28	| Brazil | ~0.5 | ~1.4% | Roughly stable |
    29	| France | ~0.3 | ~0.8% | Declining |
    30	
    31	In 1900, Europe and the US accounted for more than 90% of global emissions. By 1950, they still represented over 85%. Today, they account for less than one-third, while Asia — home to nearly 60% of the world's population — produces roughly half of all emissions. Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4%, comparable to international aviation and shipping combined.
    32	
    33	## Per Capita Emissions: Extreme Inequalities
    34	
    35	Per capita CO₂ emissions reveal stark global inequalities. The world's highest per capita emitters are major oil-producing nations with small populations (Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait). Among large, populous countries, the US, Australia, and Canada have per capita emissions roughly three times the global average.
    36	
    37	![Per capita CO₂ emissions over time](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    38	
    39	| Country | Per Capita CO₂ (tonnes/year) |
    40	|---|---|
    41	| United States | ~15 |
    42	| Canada | ~13 |
    43	| Australia | ~15 |
    44	| South Africa | ~8 |
    45	| China | ~9 |
    46	| EU-27 | ~7 |
    47	| World average | ~5 |
    48	| United Kingdom | ~4 |
    49	| France | ~4 |
    50	| India | ~2 |
    51	| Kenya | <1 |
    52	| Chad / Niger | ~0.1 |
    53	
    54	The gap between the highest and lowest per capita emitters is approximately **150-fold**: the average American or Australian emits in under two days what the average person in Chad or Niger emits in an entire year. Importantly, countries with similar living standards can differ significantly — France and the UK have much lower per capita emissions than Germany or the Netherlands, largely because of their energy mix (higher nuclear and renewable shares).
    55	
    56	## 2024 Annual Change in Emissions
    57	
    58	The 2024 map of annual percentage change in CO₂ emissions shows a mixed picture. The United States and much of Europe recorded declines (roughly −1% to −5%), shown in blue. Russia, parts of Southeast Asia, and several African nations saw increases of +2% to +10% or more, shown in orange and red. Some countries in South America (notably one or two) experienced very large percentage increases (>10%), while others saw declines.
    59	
    60	![Annual percentage change in CO₂ emissions, 2024](./assets/figure_4.jpg)
    61	
    62	## Key Findings
    63	
    64	- **Global CO₂ emissions now exceed 35 billion tonnes per year** and have not yet peaked, despite slowing growth rates.
    65	- **China alone accounts for over 25% of global emissions** (~12.5 Bt), more than double the United States (~5 Bt); India (~3 Bt) is the third-largest and rising fast.
    66	- **The geographic center of emissions has shifted dramatically**: from >90% in Europe and the US in 1900 to Asia producing ~50% today, while the US and Europe combined are below one-third.
    67	- **Per capita inequalities are extreme** — a 150× gap separates the highest emitters (US, Australia at ~15 t/person) from the lowest (Chad, Niger at ~0.1 t/person).
    68	- **Energy mix and policy choices matter**: countries with similar prosperity levels (e.g., France vs. Germany) can have very different per capita emissions depending on their reliance on nuclear, renewables, or fossil fuels.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# Create presentation 16:9
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette (dark analytical theme)
DARK_BG = RgbColor(0x1A, 0x1F, 0x2E)      # deep navy/slate
ACCENT = RgbColor(0x00, 0xC8, 0xFF)       # bright cyan
TEXT_WHITE = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)
TEXT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xB0, 0xB8, 0xC4)
MUTED = RgbColor(0x4A, 0x55, 0x6A)
HIGHLIGHT = RgbColor(0xFF, 0x6B, 0x35)    # orange accent

ASSETS = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT = "/app/output"
os.makedirs(OUTPUT, exist_ok=True)

def add_background(slide, color=DARK_BG):
    background = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height
    )
    background.fill.solid()
    background.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    background.line.fill.background()
    # Send to back
    spTree = slide.shapes._spTree
    sp = background._element
    spTree.remove(sp)
    spTree.insert(2, sp)

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18, bold=False, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return tf

def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size=16, color=TEXT_WHITE, font_name="Calibri", bullet_color=ACCENT):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(12)
    return tf

def add_accent_bar(slide, left, top, width, height, color=ACCENT):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()

def add_footer(slide, text="Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025 / NASA"):
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.4), Inches(7.1), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.3), text, font_size=10, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ============================================================
# Slide 1: Title
# ============================================================
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
add_background(slide)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(2.6), Inches(0.08), Inches(2.3), ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(2.5), Inches(11.5), Inches(1.2),
            "Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities",
            font_size=40, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(3.8), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.6),
            "A data-driven overview from the Industrial Revolution to 2024",
            font_size=22, bold=False, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.5), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
            "Data sources: Global Carbon Budget 2025  ·  NASA / NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory",
            font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_footer(slide)

# ============================================================
# Slide 2: Atmospheric CO₂ Milestone
# ============================================================
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.55), Inches(0.08), Inches(0.55), ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(0.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "Atmospheric CO₂ Reaches 429 ppm — 50% Above Pre-Industrial Levels",
            font_size=30, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Big stat callout box
box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(0.55), Inches(1.5), Inches(5.5), Inches(2.2))
box.fill.solid()
box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0x22, 0x2A, 0x3A)
box.line.color.rgb = ACCENT
box.line.width = Pt(1.5)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.7), Inches(5), Inches(0.8), "429 ppm", font_size=56, bold=True, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.6), Inches(5), Inches(0.5), "Latest NOAA Mauna Loa reading — February 2026", font_size=16, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.1), Inches(5), Inches(0.5), "> 50% increase from pre-industrial baseline of ~280 ppm", font_size=16, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Context bullets
bullets = [
    "Current level is at least 1.5× greater than the natural increase at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago.",
    "That ancient change took thousands of years; the modern rise has occurred in roughly two centuries.",
    "Ground-based and satellite measurements confirm the sharp acceleration, linked primarily to burning coal, oil, and natural gas."
]
add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(4.1), Inches(12), Inches(3), bullets, font_size=17, color=TEXT_WHITE)
add_footer(slide)

# ============================================================
# Slide 3: Global Emissions Trajectory
# ============================================================
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.55), Inches(0.08), Inches(0.55), ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(0.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "Global Fossil Fuel CO₂ Emissions Grew Six-Fold: 6 Billion to 35+ Billion Tonnes",
            font_size=30, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Timeline callouts
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(1.4), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.5), "1950", font_size=28, bold=True, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(1.85), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.5), "~6 billion tonnes", font_size=18, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(4.2), Inches(1.4), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.5), "1990", font_size=28, bold=True, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(4.2), Inches(1.85), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.5), "~20 billion tonnes", font_size=18, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(7.8), Inches(1.4), Inches(4.5), Inches(0.5), "2024", font_size=28, bold=True, color=HIGHLIGHT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(7.8), Inches(1.85), Inches(4.5), Inches(0.5), ">35 billion tonnes", font_size=18, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Chart placeholder / description
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(2.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
            "Trajectory description: line chart showing near-zero emissions before 1750, slow growth through the 19th century, steep acceleration after 1950, and continued rise to >35 Bt today.",
            font_size=14, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Try to embed figure_2 if exists (not in assets, but task says reference figure_2.jpg)
# We'll just note it as a referenced visual since file is absent.
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(3.0), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
            "Reference: figure_2.jpg — Annual global CO₂ emissions line chart (1750–2024).",
            font_size=13, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

bullets = [
    "Before the Industrial Revolution, CO₂ emissions were negligible.",
    "Growth remained relatively slow until the mid-20th century, then quadrupled by 1990.",
    "While emissions growth has slowed in recent years, they have not yet peaked."
]
add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(3.6), Inches(12), Inches(3), bullets, font_size=17, color=TEXT_WHITE)
add_footer(slide)

# ============================================================
# Slide 4: China Surpasses US
# ============================================================
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.55), Inches(0.08), Inches(0.55), ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(0.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "China Now Emits Over 12 Billion Tonnes — More Than Double the United States",
            font_size=30, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Data table
rows, cols = 9, 4
left = Inches(0.55)
top = Inches(1.4)
width = Inches(11.5)
height = Inches(3.6)
table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table

table.columns[0].width = Inches(3.0)
table.columns[1].width = Inches(3.0)
table.columns[2].width = Inches(2.5)
table.columns[3].width = Inches(3.0)

headers = ["Country / Region", "Approx. Annual CO₂ (billion t)", "Share of Global", "Trend (recent)"]
for i, h in enumerate(headers):
    cell = table.cell(0, i)
    cell.text = h
    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = MUTED

data = [
    ["China", "~12.5", "~27%", "Slight increase"],
    ["United States", "~5.0", "~14%", "Declining"],
    ["India", "~3.0", "~8%", "Rising"],
    ["EU-27", "~2.7", "~7%", "Declining"],
    ["Germany", "~0.6", "~1.7%", "Declining"],
    ["United Kingdom", "~0.3", "~0.9%", "Declining"],
    ["Brazil", "~0.5", "~1.4%", "Roughly stable"],
    ["France", "~0.3", "~0.8%", "Declining"],
]

for r, row in enumerate(data, start=1):
    for c, val in enumerate(row):
        cell = table.cell(r, c)
        cell.text = val
        cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(13)
        cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x26, 0x36)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(5.2), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
            "Reference: figure_3.jpg — Annual CO₂ emissions by country.",
            font_size=13, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

bullets = [
    "China is the world's largest emitter by a significant margin — more than one-quarter of the global total.",
    "The United States peaked near 6 billion tonnes around 2005 and has since declined to roughly 5 billion tonnes.",
    "India has risen rapidly to approximately 3 billion tonnes, becoming the third-largest emitter."
]
add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(5.6), Inches(12), Inches(1.5), bullets, font_size=16, color=TEXT_WHITE)
add_footer(slide)

# ============================================================
# Slide 5: Regional Share Shift
# ============================================================
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.55), Inches(0.08), Inches(0.55), ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(0.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "Asia Now Accounts for ~50% of Global Emissions; US + Europe Below One-Third",
            font_size=30, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Visual description
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(1.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.5),
            "Visual: stacked area or side-by-side comparison showing regional emission shares from 1900 to 2024.",
            font_size=15, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Two-column comparison
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(2.0), Inches(5.5), Inches(0.5), "1900", font_size=26, bold=True, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(2.5), Inches(5.5), Inches(2.0),
            "Europe and the US accounted for more than 90% of global CO₂ emissions.\n\nAsia, Africa, and South America represented a marginal share of the global total.",
            font_size=17, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(6.8), Inches(2.0), Inches(5.5), Inches(0.5), "2024", font_size=26, bold=True, color=HIGHLIGHT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(6.8), Inches(2.5), Inches(5.5), Inches(2.5),
